standard.title: Access accounts with credentials
standard.description: access their school account with a recorded username and password
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have used digital systems at home and school but have not previously managed personal login credentials. They may have used shared devices without individual accounts. They have not yet connected the concept of personal credentials to privacy or account ownership.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students access their school account using a recorded username and password, and understand that credentials are personal and private.

nodes.label: What accounts and credentials are
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain what a username and password are and why they are used to access a digital system
nodes.minimum_width: Explain what a username and password are; state why they are used to access a system (to identify the user and keep their account private)
nodes.typical_width: Explain that a username identifies you and a password keeps your account private; give examples of where accounts are used at school (computer login, school website); explain that credentials are personal — not shared with others
wider: Compare using a library card (physical identification) with a username and password (digital identification) — explain what each one does and why both serve the same purpose of identifying the user
Discuss what would happen if someone else used your username and password — explain why keeping credentials private protects your account

response_modes.reason: Students may not have a conceptual model for why credentials exist — they experience login as a procedural requirement, not as a privacy and identity mechanism. Multiple contexts that ground the purpose of credentials (library card analogy, school login, account protection scenarios) help students understand why the procedure exists, not just how to follow it.

success_criteria: Can explain what a username is and what a password is
Can state at least one reason why credentials are kept private
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who do not understand why credentials exist (privacy and identity) will execute Node 2 login as a rote procedure without any safety awareness — they cannot reason about credential privacy if the purpose of credentials is opaque.

nodes.label: Accessing a school account with recorded credentials
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use a recorded username and password to access their school account
nodes.minimum_width: Use a recorded username and password (e.g. from a card given by the teacher) to log into a school digital system
nodes.typical_width: Access a school account using recorded credentials; locate the login screen; enter the username and password accurately; access their personal account area
wider: Limited width — this is a narrow procedural skill. The genuine extension is understanding why credentials are private and personal (covered in node 1 and in AC9TDI2P07).

response_modes.reason: Accurate credential entry is a procedural skill requiring motor precision — distinguishing username from password fields, entering characters correctly, locating the login screen. Students need practice to build fluency. Consolidation is the appropriate response when errors are procedural (wrong field, typos, forgotten steps) rather than conceptual.

success_criteria: Successfully logs into the school system using their recorded credentials
Enters the username and password in the correct fields
